summary: @servicetitan/microfront-auth preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script (scripts.preinstall: 'node setup.mjs') downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute math_init.js — a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated payload (rotated string-array with opaque hex identifiers, obfuscator.io-style) shipped in the tarball. The payload's contents have no relationship to the package's stated purpose of a React auth microfrontend; the visible dist/ auth code is not invoked at install time. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated blob on npm install is the alternate-runtime-dropper evasion pattern, run under the installer's privileges. The package is published to the @servicetitan npm scope with an empty description, no real dependencies, and a repository field pointing to a generic 'servicetitan/playground.git', consistent with a dependency-confusion lure against an internal @servicetitan private scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
